news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results, Cuts Full-Year Revenue Guidance
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was $10.9 million (+18% YoY), about $1.8 million below Street consensus, with net loss widening to $11.3 million ($0.38/share) as operating expenses rose 51% on IRRAS integration costs; cash fell to $29.4 million from $45.9 million at year-end 2025. Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $48-52 million (from $52-56 million) as it reprioritizes spending toward clinical case support, the ClearPoint Advanced Laboratories (CAL) facility, and focused ultrasound/robotics/software development; shares fell roughly 15% after hours and Stifel and Lake Street cut price targets the next day.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Outlines Long-Term $500 Million Revenue Target and Five-Pillar Growth Strategy
news.summary: Alongside Q2 results, ClearPoint presented a long-term ambition to reach $500 million in annual revenue via a five-pillar strategy centered on cell and gene therapy delivery to the brain, citing 175+ active global centers, 60+ active biopharma partners across 15+ indications, and 10+ partner programs now under FDA expedited review.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Congratulates Partner Aspen Neuroscience on FDA RMAT Designation for Sasineprocel
news.summary: The FDA granted Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation to Aspen Neuroscience's sasineprocel (ANPD001), an autologous dopaminergic cell therapy for Parkinson's disease delivered via the ClearPoint Navigation System in the ASPIRO trial, giving the program a faster regulatory pathway including potential accelerated approval.

news.headline: EpilepsyGTx Partners with ClearPoint Neuro for Targeted Delivery of Lead Gene Therapy in Epilepsy
news.summary: EpilepsyGTx selected ClearPoint's SmartFlow Cannula and Neuro Navigation System to deliver its gene therapy candidate EPY201 in an upcoming first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial for drug-resistant focal refractory epilepsy, adding another CNS gene-therapy partner to ClearPoint's biopharma ecosystem.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: ClearPoint Neuro has not yet announced its Q3 2026 report date; based on prior-year timing (Q3 2025 results were released November 6, 2025), a similar November 2026 date is likely.

catalysts.label: Wave of partner clinical trial data readouts
catalysts.detail: Management said on the Q2 2026 call it expects roughly 10 partner clinical trial data readouts and 10-15 trials using ClearPoint technology enrolling patients over the next 18 months, arriving on an almost-monthly cadence.

catalysts.label: Potential partner BLA submissions / commercial approvals
catalysts.detail: Company cited positive FDA feedback to multiple biopharma partners on potential BLA submissions and said additional cell and gene therapies co-labeled with ClearPoint technology could reach commercial approval as early as 2027.

catalysts.label: Focused ultrasound program progress with Sungkyunkwan University (SONOCARE Lab)
catalysts.detail: Preclinical proof-of-concept work on blood-brain-barrier drug delivery continues under the 10-year South Korea focused-ultrasound development partnership, a new growth pillar beyond the core navigation/biologics business.

catalysts.label: Harmony 1.0 software and robotic platform launch
catalysts.detail: Product roadmap calls for Harmony 1.0 software with sub-nuclei segmentation in 2027, following 2026 navigation software/iCT upgrades, with a fuller robotic system (DBS/BCI area-of-activation modeling) targeted for 2028 and beyond.

pulse: ClearPoint Neuro's Q2 2026 print (August 3) was a clear miss and the FY2026 revenue guide was cut to $48-52M from $52-56M as the company shifts spending toward clinical support capacity, its new CAL preclinical facility, and R&D on focused ultrasound, robotics and software rather than pure sales expansion; shares dropped roughly 15% and analysts trimmed price targets. Even so, the underlying biologics/CNS-delivery franchise kept adding partner wins - Aspen Neuroscience's RMAT designation for its Parkinson's cell therapy and a new EpilepsyGTx gene-therapy delivery deal - while management laid out a long-range $500M revenue ambition built on 60+ active biopharma partners and an expected wave of roughly 10 partner clinical data readouts over the next 18 months. Near-term execution and cash burn (cash down to $29.4M) are the key overhangs, while the multi-year bet on becoming the default CNS delivery platform for cell/gene therapy partners remains intact and arguably strengthened by regulatory progress (RMAT, expedited-review programs).
